'''Michael Herzog''' (born 1964) is a German [[neuroscientist]] and [[Psychophysics|psychophysicist]]. His interdisciplinary research draws on [[biology]], [[neuroscience]]s, mathematics, and philosophy with a focus on [[perception]]. Herzog is a professor for neuroscience at the School of Life Sciences at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and head of the Laboratory of Psychophysics.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Strategic topics with a focus on the next performance period {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/medien-medienmitteilungen/strategie-entwicklung-im-zeichen-der-n%C3%A4chsten-leistungsperiode|access-date=2020-10-14|website=www.ethrat.ch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Michael Herzog|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lpsy/team/herzog/|access-date=2020-10-14|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Career ==
Herzog studied mathematics, [[biology]] and philosophy at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg|University of Erlangen]], at the [[University of Tübingen]], and at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). In 1992, he received a diploma in mathematics from the [[University of Tübingen]] for his thesis on "Automorphism groups of [[Hamming graph]]s" supervised by [[Christoph Hering]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/147878|title=Automorphism groups of Hamming Graphs|date=1992|publisher=University of Tübingen|editor-last=Herzog|editor-first=Michael H.}}</ref> In 1993, Herzog earned a master's degree in philosophy from the [[University of Tübingen]] for his research with [[Herbert Keuth]] about approaches to intentionality and representation. He then joined [[Manfred Fahle]] at the [[University of Tübingen]] and [[Tomaso Poggio]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and earned a PhD in biology for his thesis on "mathematical models and psychophysical experiments of perceptual learning".<ref>{{Cite book|title=Perceptual learning|date=2002|publisher=MIT Press|others=Fahle, Manfred., Poggio, Tomaso.|isbn=978-0-262-27246-9|location=Cambridge, Mass.|oclc=51968804}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Herzog|first1=Michael H.|last2=Fahle|first2=Manfred|date=1 February 1998|title=Modeling perceptual learning: difficulties and how they can be overcome|journal=Biological Cybernetics|volume=78|issue=2|pages=107–117|doi=10.1007/s004220050418|pmid=9525037|s2cid=12351107|issn=0340-1200}}</ref>

From 1998 to 1999, he joined the laboratory of [[Christof Koch]] at [[California Institute of Technology]] as a postdoctoral fellow to investigating the characteristics of temporal processing and feature integration. In 1999, he went to work as a senior researcher with [[Manfred Fahle]] at the section of Human Neurobiology at the [[University of Bremen]] where he was project  leader at the Center of Excellence 517 on "Neurocognition" that was funded by [[German Research Council]] (DFG).<ref>{{Cite journal|date=1 August 2001|title=Shine-through: temporal aspects|journal=Vision Research|language=en|volume=41|issue=18|pages=2337–2346|doi=10.1016/S0042-6989(01)00123-7|issn=0042-6989|last1=Herzog|first1=Michael H.|last2=Koch|first2=Christof|last3=Fahle|first3=Manfred|pmid=11459591|s2cid=5066600|doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2003 he became a professor for [[Neuropsychology|neurobiopsychology]] at the [[Osnabrück University]] for one year.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Michael Herzog|url=https://www.uni-bielefeld.de/(de)/ZiF/FG/2019Behavior/Members/mherzog.html|access-date=2020-10-16|website=www.uni-bielefeld.de|language=en}}</ref>

In 2004, Herzog was appointed as professor for neuroscience at the Brain Mind Institute of the School of Life Sciences at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] and head of the Laboratory of Psychophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LPSY – Laboratory of Psychophysics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lpsy/|access-date=2020-10-15|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> In 2015, he was promoted as Full Professor at EPFL.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==

Herzog's laboratory investigates visual information processing in humans applying psychophysical methods, [[Transcranial magnetic stimulation|TMS]], [[Electroencephalography|EEG]], and [[mathematical modelling]]. Their research focuses on feature integration, contextual modulation, time course of information processing, and perceptual learning.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Overney|first1=Leila
